pagerbot: PagerDuty incident PD-87432 created and routed to eng-sre. Acknowledge with `/pd ack PD-87432` or respond in-thread.

alex: I'm on it, looking at Prometheus target statuses now. seeing `DOWN` for exporter-node-metrics across a few hosts.

sam: pulling exporter logs from host-12 and host-15, getting repeated OOM and TCP timeout: `killed by OOM` then long GC pauses.

alex: can you paste the last 50 lines?

sam: ```
May 12 10:02:41 exporter[pid=2134]: runtime: out of memory
May 12 10:02:41 exporter[pid=2134]: panic: runtime: out of memory

May 12 10:03:45 exporter[pid=2147]: slow response, scrape latency 12s
```

maria: /pd ack PD-87432 — taking lead for oncall handoff. tagging @alex and @sam. quick status: customers report dashboards missing host-level CPU metrics but no product outage reported. Affected: dashboards and some autoscaling alarms.

alex: thanks. hypothesis: exporter memory leak under high cardinality around 10:00, causing crash loop and scrape timeouts -> Prometheus marks targets DOWN -> metric gap. Also noticed logdrain backlog in ingestion (kafka consumer lag creeping up) starting ~10:05. may be correlated (spike in telemetry).

sam: restarted exporter on host-12 and host-15 manually, keeping watch. immediate uptick in scrape success for those two. still a handful of hosts flapping.

alex: can we temporarily remove the most expensive metrics from the exporter scrape to reduce mem pressure? quick config tweak: set `metrics_filter` to exclude `process_open_fds` and high-cardinality labels.

maria: good idea. sam, can you push a scoped config change to scrape-proxy `exporter-lite` via canary (single region) and monitor? link to runbook: https://runbooks/internal/exporter-memory-issues

sam: rolling canary now: `kubectl apply -f exporter-lite-configmap --context=prod`

incidentbot: Monitoring rule fired: log_ingest_consumer_lag > 1000 for kafka-group log-consumers — started backlog counter.

alex: that log backlog might be from the crash loop generating reconnect storms. if we don't clear it, S3 uploader will throttle and increase downstream latencies. we should scale log-consumers by +2 replicas temporarily.

maria: agreed. sam, can you scale the consumer statefulset? `kubectl scale sts/log-consumers --replicas=6` and watch partition assignment.

sam: scaled to 6. watching rebalances. partition lag decreasing slowly.

jordan: ping — I'll be taking over in ~40m. any blockers I should know about?

maria: handoff note for @jordan: root cause likely exporter OOMs (possible memory regression in v1.4.2). mitigations applied: manual restarts, exporter-lite config canary, scaled log consumers to handle backlog. PD incident acknowledged and oncall engaged. still seeing ~2 hosts flapping; next steps: rollout exporter-lite config cluster-wide if canary stable, investigate heap usage in v1.4.2, open PR to revert last bump if confirmed. customer impact: dashboards showing partial gaps for ~15 mins, no API outages.

alex: observed scrape success rate climbed from 68% -> 94% after restarts + canary. logs show S3 PUT throttling still present, throttles decreasing.

sam: can confirm kafka lag down 60% since scale. starting backfill job to replay ~200k events: `kafka-backfill --topic logs-raw --from-offset 123456 --to-latest` — kicked off. ETA ~12m.

pagerbot: PD-87432 status updated: acknowledged by maria. Assigned to eng-sre.

jordan: thanks — I'll monitor the rest of the window and take over clean-up. leaving a short checklist for the next oncall: [ ] verify canary for 15m, [ ] if stable, rollout exporter-lite to all nodes via rollout job, [ ] inspect heap dump from host-15, [ ] file regression ticket against exporter v1.4.2 and link heap dump.

maria: adding customer notification draft: "We observed a temporary gap in host-level metrics for ~15 minutes due to an internal exporter process instability. Metrics are restored; we are investigating root cause and will follow up with findings." will send after handoff. :thumbsup:
